second most abundant free AA in their brain and liver (Table 1). Human skeletal muscle, heart, retina, placenta, brain, and small-
intestinal mucosa contain 15–20, 28–40, 20–35, 20–35, 1.16, and 8.74 mM taurine, respectively (Wu, 2020). A healthy 70-kg
person has approximately 80 g glutamine and 70 g taurine. In the human brain and small-intestinal mucosa, glutamate is the
most abundant and second most abundant free AA, respectively. Interestingly, aspartate is the most abundant free AA in the human
liver (Table 1). Selenocysteine does not occur as a free AA in humans (Wu, 2022).
Peptide- (or protein)-bound AAs are those AAs that are linked in peptides or proteins via peptide bonds. A healthy 70-kg adult
human contains 15.1% protein (or 10.6 kg protein), including 3.72 kg collagen or 35% of the total body protein. Skeletal muscle
contains about 20% protein and accounts for 45% of body mass in non-obese and non-overweight heathy adults. In skeletal
muscle proteins, glutamate is the most abundant amino acid, followed by leucine, lysine, and arginine. In the whole body, glycine
is the most abundant amino acid, followed by proline, glutamate, and arginine in descending order (Table 1). Note that seleno-
